pr_title: sql: No-op GRANT/ROVOKE/ALTER ROLE that are no-ops
pr_body:
Previously, we schedule a schema change for every 'GRANT', 'REVOKE',
or 'ALTER ROLE' statements even if they are no-ops, that is, if they
don't actually change any
  1. privileges (via `GRANT/REVOKE privileges ...`), or
  2. role memberships (via `GRANT/REVOKE role ...`), or
  3. role options (via `ALTER ROLE ... WITH ...`), or
  4. default session vars values(via `ALTER ROLE ... SET/RESET ...`)

Performing a schema change on such no-op statements will invalidate
caches and hence incur overhead. This PR fixes this by detecting those
no-ops and make them real no-op (i.e. no schema change will be
performed) and consequently avoid unnecessary cache invalidation.

fixes: #77500 

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/81128)

issue_context.title: sql: no-op ALTER ROLE/ GRANTS that are no-ops
issue_context.body:
Currently, we still invalidate caches for these schema changes even when they are a no-op. This is a fairly easy win that can avoid certain headaches since we don't need to bump up table versions or carry out any other operations. In the case of authorization/security-related schema changes, no-ops can be a huge win since caches that will impact all query workloads will not get invalidated.

Jira issue: CRDB-13623
